album: Layla and Other Assorted Love Songs

position_in_era.historical_role: The first canonical rock song built on two entirely separate movements: a volcanic guitar-and-vocal section followed by a completely distinct, tranquil piano coda — two protagonists (Clapton/Allman guitar; Gordon piano) inhabiting the same piece without sharing a foreground.

narrative_slots.production_facts: First section recorded September 9, 1970; piano coda recorded roughly a week later at Criteria Studios, Miami. Sixteen tracks for the main section including six guitar tracks. Both Clapton and Allman overdubbed their slide and lead parts separately.
narrative_slots.member_dynamics: Eric Clapton (vocal, lead guitar) and Duane Allman (slide guitar) function as dual guitar protagonists in the first movement, their lines intertwining in the 'anguished duet.' Jim Gordon's piano coda is a structurally independent second movement — a different emotional protagonist entering after Clapton exits. Bobby Whitlock (organ, harmony vocals) and Carl Radle (bass) complete the band.
narrative_slots.instrumentation_details: Clapton: Fender Stratocaster and Gibson SG. Allman: Gibson ES-335 with Coricidin bottle slide. Gordon: acoustic piano for coda. The six guitar overdub tracks in the main section create a dense textural foreground where two distinct voices (Clapton's bends, Allman's slide) are simultaneously audible.
narrative_slots.cultural_venue: Criteria Studios, Miami — the same studio where the Allmans and CSNY had recently recorded, giving the session a fluid, jamming energy. The two movements were originally intended as separate pieces; Clapton heard Gordon's piano sketch and insisted on appending it.
narrative_slots.release_circumstances: Album released November 1970. The single became one of rock's most celebrated songs but was initially a commercial failure, charting only after Clapton's identity as Derek was publicly revealed.
